Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@strandai.com>; procurement@strandai.com
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — projected tokens/sec & p95 fit

Irene — thanks again for the call last week. We got internal buy-in to explore dedicated capacity for our new multi-turn summarization pipeline but procurement needs concrete numbers for: tokens/sec steady state, burst headroom, expected p95 latencies at our target model sizes, and a recommended GPU slab for the first 12 months.

Attaching a CSV with sample traffic traces (hourly token counts) and a short MAAP deck. High level constraints:
- Primary region: us-west-2
- Initial commit target: 60M tokens / month
- Traffic shape: daily peak at 2.5x baseline, occasional marketing-driven bursts up to 6x for <2 hours
- Model: we expect to serve a mix of a 7B chat-optimized model for short queries and a 13B summarization model for long-form (avg seq len 1,800 tokens)

Can you propose a throughput and latency model (tokens/sec per slab), recommended slab size (GPU type + count), and an SLO hedging plan (burst buffer + graceful degradation)? Procurement would like something we can fold into a TCO worksheet.

Thanks,
Laura
Director of Platform
StrandAI

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — projected tokens/sec & p95 fit

Laura — thanks for the traces, this is great. High-level reply below; I'll follow up with a short spreadsheet that maps tokens/sec to candidate slabs and p95 latency estimates. Ben and Kim are looped in for sizing + pricing.

Quick take:
- Short model (7B chat): ~80-140 tokens/sec per A100-80GB slab with our inference config (int8-ish profile, 512-context optimizations). P95 ~70-120ms for 1-2 turn chat.
- Long model (13B summarizer, avg 1800 tokens): effective throughput falls because of long sequences and KV cache pressure — expect ~6-12 tokens/sec per A100-80GB slab if we target p95 < 3s for synthesize flows; p95 can jump to ~6s under high concurrency without batching knobs.

Headroom approach:
1) Base slab to cover commit: we model tokens/month -> tokens/sec steady-state using your hourly trace median; for 60M/mo with StrandAI's shape, baseline TLS ~ 25 tokens/sec sustained across peak hours (I will show math).
2) Burst buffer: recommend a dedicated reserved buffer equal to 2x baseline slab capacity for 90-day rolling bursts (fast failover to compute pool).
3) Graceful degradation: prefer response-length caps on summarizer (drop 1800 -> 1200 when burst) and fall back to cached summaries for repeat queries to preserve latency SLOs.

I'll attach an internal workbook with mapping assumptions (kernel latency, seq-length penalty factors, throughput per GPU). If that all sounds good I can produce a 12-month committed slab plan (counts by GPU SKU) and an ops playbook for KV warmup/caching.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

[Attachment: RI_SLA_optimal_slab_proposal_v3.pdf (pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — projected tokens/sec & p95 fit

Irene — I ran a couple of microbenchmarks against the 13B summarizer (fp16 + per-layer fusers and KV caching) and here's what I observed (local sim, 2 concurrent requests per GPU):
- seq=1800, batch=1: 10-13 tokens/sec, mean per-token latency ~90ms (p95 jump on tails ~180ms due to attention tiling)
- seq=1800, batching via batching window 30ms (2–4 queued): ~18–22 tokens/sec, p95 ~450–600ms because of queuing + memory pressure

Implication: slab recommendations depend on how much latency SLAs you accept for summarizer flows and whether you allow short batching windows. For StrandAI's p95 target of <3s we're safe with 3–4 A100-80GBs dedicated (for production summarizer fleet per peak unit). If they want <1s p95, we need more aggressive slabting + KV prewarm and possibly move to H100 or pruned 14B quantized profile.

I attached a quick table mapping tokens/sec to slab counts for both models and example cost estimates (commit vs burst on-demand).

— Ben
Principal Inference Eng — Redwood Inference

Laura/Samir — following up with the TCO sensitivity and documented SLO behavior you asked for. Summary below and I attached a short TCO worksheet.

TCO sensitivity (12-month reserved for summarizer workload):
- Option A (3x A100-80GB reserved): covers expected steady-state + 1.5x burst headroom; estimated committed cost $62k/mo; estimated effective cost ~ $0.46 /1k tokens (assumes caching reduces token re-generation by 9%).
- Option B (4x A100-80GB reserved): covers steady-state + 3x burst headroom; estimated committed cost $81k/mo; effective cost ~ $0.37 /1k tokens (lower because of utilization smoothing).
- Option C (3x H100 reserved, mixed instance): estimated committed cost $99k/mo; effective cost ~ $0.29 /1k tokens, but note H100 amortizes better on p95 targets <1s — requires validation for your long sequences (we'd run a pilot).

SLO fallback behavior (ops playbook):
1) If observed cluster utilization > 95% for sustained 10+ minutes, traffic beyond reserved capacity is redirected to a pre-provisioned shared on-demand pool and served on quantized 14B variant with best-effort latency; we mark responses with a response_metadata flag indicating fallback.
2) For 6x marketing bursts: automated throttles kick in after 5 minutes to enforce per-account concurrency and length caps (we recommend 1200-token cap on summarizer during burst).
3) KV cache warmup: we recommend a 2-hour warmup window pre-burst if known in advance; otherwise expect initial p95 degradation for first ~30 minutes as caches populate.

Action items:
- I'll share the attached TCO workbook (MAAP_estimates_StrandAI.xlsx) and a short SLA appendix describing fallback response indicators.
- If StrandAI is comfortable with Option A or B, we can draft a reserved capacity statement of work and a 30-day pilot for H100 validation if you want to test that path.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through the worksheet with procurement.

Aditya Rao
Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
